data.title: Add absolute q/p term to the initial track covariance
data.author: jburzy
data.body:
`makeInitialCovariance` sets the initial q/p error to `InitialTrackError_RelP / p`, which is purely relative. For high pT seeds this is very small in absolute terms (0.005 e/GeV at 50 GeV with the default of 0.25), while the curvature estimate from three closely spaced hits can be much worse, especially in forward regions. The CKF then cannot correct the momentum, and good hits further out fail the chi2 cut. Raising `InitialTrackError_RelP` frees the high pT seeds but also lets soft seeds drift, so fake tracks migrate to high pT.

This adds `InitialTrackError_QOverP` to `CKFTrackingAlg` and `GNNTrackFinder`. It is an absolute q/p error added in quadrature to the relative one, similar to the absolute term in `Acts::estimateTrackParamCovariance`. It barely changes the error of soft seeds a…

data.title: Fix the orientation of the hit covariance in `prepareTrackerHits`
data.author: jburzy
data.body:
The hit position is converted into the local frame of the ACTS surface, but `du`/`dv` were assigned directly to loc0/loc1. They are defined along the hit's own u/v axes, which do not always match the surface's local x/y. In the MAIA IT/OT endcaps the two are swapped, so the precise direction got the large uncertainty and the coarse direction got the small one. Good endcap hits then failed the CKF chi2 cut, which led to holes and truncated or lost forward tracks.

The new `hitLocalCovariance` rotates diag(du², dv²) from the hit's u/v axes into the surface frame (`Surface::referenceFrame`). The 4D measurement uses the full rotated 2x2 block. Barrel modules are unchanged, since there u/v already match the local axes.

This is a proposed long-term fix for the problem described in this ticket (and several tickets):

data.author: davidlange6

Three inner loops each iterated over all MCParticles to find non-zero entries, giving O(N_hits × N_particles) and O(N_cluster_hits × N_links) complexity.

primary changes: 1) Iterate simHitMapEnergy map keys directly instead of scanning all MCParticles for non-zero entries. 2)Build a cellID → links index (std::unordered_map) once after the calo-hit loop, then use O(1) lookup per cluster hit instead of a full scan of the link collection. 3) Iiterate mcpEnergy map keys directly instead of scanning all MCParticles per cluster.

## Summary

This PR improves dashboard performance by avoiding repeated loading and parsing of nightly regression reports, while also reducing memory usage and simplifying some of the data processing.

Previously, reports were cached as raw JSON and parsed independently by different dashboard tabs. Reports are now parsed once per night and cached as `NightlyReport` objects using `st.cache_resource`. This allows different tabs and overlapping date ranges to reuse the same parsed data without repeating the work.
